action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's call is to scale up the acquisition budget: the longer-term trend and the last three months both lean up, with high confidence (85/100 after today's news, 81 on market data alone), so this remains a reasonable time to fund growth, weighted toward channels that bring active traders rather than stablecoin-only users. Because price is sitting right on its 50-day average ($81,815) with the Fed meeting starting 27 October, add budget in steps and keep part of it flexible to pause if price closes below $81,416 (the 30-day low). This is a budget posture based on trailing data, not a price call or trading advice.

A close below $81,416 (the 30-day low) would test the uptrend; a close back above $86,480 would ease the worry.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger trend still leans up, but this week Bitcoin is sitting right on a floor that matters. Short term, the mood is only mildly positive: Fear & Greed is a middling 50 out of 100 and price is up just 0.4% over the past week, sitting near about $81,000, which Glassnode (via PANews) says is roughly what the average US Bitcoin fund buyer paid. News is taking a little off the mood: a broad tech-stock sell-off tied to worries about AI-company debt, and a disputed security incident at Indian exchange CoinDCX (both PANews). If price closes above $86,480 (the 30-day high) the short term turns clearly up; below $81,416 (the 30-day low) it turns down, and in between expect choppy days; a close below that low would call for a more careful, trust-first tone.

Over the next month, the picture still leans moderately up. Price is about 27% higher than three months ago and about 73% of the last 90 days finished above the long-term average, but it now sits only a hair above the 50-day average. There is room to climb if price gets above $86,603 (the 90-day high); the move fades if it closes below $81,815 (the 50-day average). The Fed meeting starting 27 October is the next scheduled event: holding the 50-day line through it keeps growth campaigns well timed, while a slip below would argue for slowing new spend.

Over three to six months, the trend leans up with the most confidence of the three. Price is about 12% above its 200-day average, which is still rising slowly, and about a third below its record, so this reads as an early recovery rather than a mature uptrend. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $72,866 (the 200-day average), with $67,152 (the 200-week average) as the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high) as the far marker. Banks keep building on crypto rails, with SoFi launching insured tokenized deposits for everyday customers (PANews); a faster-rising 200-day average would strengthen this read and support steady investment in new-user acquisition.
